input.strategy_title: Feature Store as a supported RHOAI component
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Customers building recommendation and fraud models ask for a supported feature
store; today they self-manage upstream Feast next to the platform with no
lifecycle integration, no supported images, and no UI presence. Feast has a
Jira component reserved (Feature Store) but is not yet part of the platform:
there is no productized repository, no build pipeline, and no operator
integration. This strategy brings Feast in as a supported, installable RHOAI
component.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can enable a supported Feature Store (Feast) through the Platform Operator like any other managed component, with productized images. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Data scientists can reach the feature store from workbenches with the Feast SDK preinstalled in at least one supported workbench image. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard shows the Feature Store as an enabled component and links users to its endpoints per project. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Product documentation covers enablement, a getting-started walkthrough, and supported limits. |

## Affected Components

- Feature Store
- Dashboard
- Platform Operator
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- A feature-authoring UI in the Dashboard (link-out only this release)
- Managed offline-store infrastructure — customers bring their own storage

## Open Questions

1. Which Feast deployment topology do we productize first — the operator-based
   deployment or the standalone server per project? Upstream supports both;
   supportability differs.

# Productize the Feast operator-based deployment (branch A)

## Description

For the outcome where the deployment topology investigation selects the
operator-based deployment: productize the Feast operator-based deployment from
the midstream repository, so the Platform Operator can manage the Feature
Store lifecycle through the operator. This epic exists only if the
operator-based topology is selected.

## Scope

- Package the operator-based deployment artifacts from the midstream Feast
  repository (operator image and deployment manifests) so the Feature Store
  lifecycle is managed by the operator.
- Validate lifecycle operations through the operator: install, upgrade, and
  removal of Feature Store instances.
- Ensure the artifacts build through the repository's Konflux build pipeline.
- Make pinned image digests available for the Platform Operator integration
  to reference (configuration reference, not a scheduling dependency).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The operator-based deployment artifacts build green in the Konflux build
  pipeline.
- Lifecycle operations (install, upgrade, removal) are validated through the
  operator.
- A pinned digest of the productized Feast server image is referenced by the
  deployment artifacts rather than a floating tag.
- The artifacts are ready for the Platform Operator to manage as the Feature
  Store deployment mechanism.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): administrators enable the supported Feature Store through the
  Platform Operator, deployed via the operator-based topology.

## Risks / Notes

- This epic is removed if the investigation selects the standalone per-project
  server topology; deployment productization is then covered by the per-project
  server branch instead.

# Productize the standalone per-project Feast server deployment (branch B)

## Description

For the outcome where the deployment topology investigation selects the
standalone server per project: productize a project-scoped Feast server
deployment from the midstream repository, with a per-project endpoint and
configuration for customer-provided offline-store storage. This epic exists
only if the standalone per-project topology is selected.

## Scope

- Define the per-project Feast server deployment artifacts from the midstream
  repository: project-scoped server instances with a per-project endpoint.
- Support configuration of customer-provided offline-store storage (managed
  offline-store infrastructure is out of scope — customers bring their own
  storage).
- Ensure the artifacts build through the repository's Konflux build pipeline.
- Make pinned image digests available for the Platform Operator integration
  to reference (configuration reference, not a scheduling dependency).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The per-project server deployment artifacts build green in the Konflux
  build pipeline.
- A project-scoped Feast server can be stood up with customer-provided
  offline-store configuration and a reachable per-project endpoint.
- A pinned digest of the productized Feast server image is referenced by the
  deployment artifacts rather than a floating tag.
- The artifacts are ready for the Platform Operator to manage as the Feature
  Store deployment mechanism.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): administrators enable the supported Feature Store through the
  Platform Operator, deployed as standalone per-project servers.

## Risks / Notes

- This epic is removed if the investigation selects the operator-based
  topology; deployment productization is then covered by the operator-based
  branch instead.

# Select the Feast deployment topology to productize

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's open question: which Feast deployment
topology RHOAI productizes first — the operator-based deployment or the standalone
server per project. Upstream Feast supports both; their supportability
characteristics (lifecycle management, upgrade path, per-project isolation, resource
footprint, alignment with how the Platform Operator manages other components)
differ. The outcome determines the shape of the Platform Operator integration and
the Dashboard endpoint surfacing, and selects between the two conditional
deployment-productization branches in this decomposition.

## Scope

- Define evaluation criteria for both topologies: lifecycle management (install,
  upgrade, rollback), per-project isolation, resource footprint, operational
  supportability, and alignment with the Platform Operator's managed-component model.
- Gather evidence: review upstream Feast documentation and source for both
  deployment modes, and exercise Feast locally (SDK and server) where possible to
  validate assumptions.
- Produce a decision record that names the selected topology with the
  supportability rationale, and records the consequences for the Platform Operator
  integration and the per-project endpoint model.
- Obtain stakeholder confirmation of the selection (product/support sign-off).
- Update the scope of the downstream gated work to match the selected outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision record exists that names exactly one selected topology
  (operator-based or standalone per-project server).
- Both topologies are assessed against the defined evaluation criteria, with the
  evidence cited for each.
- The decision record states what the selection means for the Platform Operator
  integration scope and the per-project endpoint model used by the Dashboard.
- The selection has been reviewed and confirmed by the accountable stakeholders.
- The downstream gated epics' scopes have been reconciled with the selected
  outcome.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): gates the approach by which administrators enable the supported
  Feature Store through the Platform Operator.

# Create midstream Feast repository under opendatahub-io

## Description

Establish the productized midstream repository for Feast under opendatahub-io.
Today customers self-manage upstream Feast with no productized repository; this
repo is the foundation for the productized server image, the SDK package, and the
deployment artifacts that the rest of the strategy builds.

## Scope

- Create the midstream repository under the opendatahub-io organization.
- Import upstream Feast content and establish the branch / backport policy used
  by other productized components.
- Add repository basics: licensing and provenance documentation, contribution
  and sync workflow with upstream, and enough CI to validate contributions
  (the Konflux build pipeline is onboarded separately and in parallel with the
  productization work).
- Grant the owning team and required automation access to the repository.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The midstream Feast repository exists under opendatahub-io with upstream
  content imported at a recorded base version.
- The upstream sync / backport workflow is documented in the repository.
- The owning team and automation have the access they need; the repository is
  clonable and buildable from source.
- Repository licensing and provenance documentation is in place.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): productized images and operator integration require a productized
  repository as their source.

# License validation for Feast and transitive dependencies

## Scope

- Run license scans over the Feast server and the Feast SDK, including their
  full transitive dependency trees.
- Identify licenses that are incompatible with shipping productized container
  images and bundling the SDK in supported workbench images.
- Produce a remediation path for every flagged dependency: an approved license
  exception, a dependency replacement, or an escalation with a recommendation.
- Record results so the image productization, operator integration, and
  workbench image work can proceed against a known-good dependency set.

## Description

Feast and its transitive dependencies have never been license-vetted for
inclusion in the platform. Before productized images are built, the SDK is
bundled into workbench images, and the Platform Operator references the
artifacts, the dependency tree must be validated so a license failure does not
surface after the fact and force a dependency change across all downstream
implementations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A scan report exists covering the Feast server and the Feast SDK dependency
  trees, including transitive dependencies.
- Every flagged license has a recorded disposition: approved exception,
  replacement dependency, or escalation with a recommendation.
- No unresolved license blockers remain for shipping the productized images or
  bundling the Feast SDK in a supported workbench image.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): productized images must be license-clean.
- HLR-2 (P1): the SDK bundled into workbench images must be license-clean.

# Productize the Feast server image and SDK package

## Description

From the midstream Feast repository, produce the supported Feast artifacts: the
productized Feast server container image and the Feast SDK package that
workbench images will bundle. This epic is topology-independent — both
deployment topologies run a Feast server from these artifacts.

## Scope

- Define the productized Feast server container image in the midstream
  repository (image content, configuration surface, and productized-image
  requirements such as running as non-root and provenance metadata).
- Define how the Feast SDK package is built and versioned from the midstream
  repository so workbench images and customers consume a supported, pinned
  version.
- Ensure both artifacts build through the repository's Konflux build pipeline.
- Record the artifact versions and make the pinned image digest available for
  consumption by the Platform Operator integration and the deployment
  artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Feast server container image builds green in the Konflux build pipeline.
- The Feast SDK package builds from the midstream repository at a pinned,
  documented version.
- A pinned image digest for the productized Feast server image is available
  for downstream consumers to reference.
- The image and package satisfy productized-artifact requirements
  (non-root execution, provenance, documented version).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): administrators get a supported Feature Store with productized
  images.
- HLR-2 (P1): the SDK package consumed by workbench images originates here.

# Enable Feature Store as a managed component in the Platform Operator

## Description

Make the Feature Store (Feast) enableable through the Platform Operator like
any other managed RHOAI component: administrators toggle it on, the operator
reconciles the selected deployment mechanism, and toggling it off removes it.
The scope of the reconciliation follows the deployment topology decision —
operator-based deployment versus standalone server per project — which is why
this epic is gated on that investigation.

## Scope

- Add the Feature Store to the Platform Operator's set of managed components
  with an administrator-facing enablement control, consistent with how other
  managed components are enabled.
- Implement reconciliation of the deployment mechanism selected by the
  topology decision: managing the operator-based deployment, or standing up
  the per-project server deployment.
- Reference the productized Feast artifacts by pinned image digest (the digest

# Feature Store as a supported RHOAI component — Decomposition Summary

Parent strategy: RHAISTRAT-9006 (Feature Store as a supported RHOAI component, priority Major, status Refinement Done).

The strategy brings Feast in as a supported, installable RHOAI component. Feast is a
**new component**: it has a reserved Jira component (`Feature Store`) but no productized
repository, no build pipeline, and no operator integration, and it has **no architecture
context file** — so Rule 20 generates a full onboarding chain (`repo-onboarding` +
`license-validation` parallel start → `konflux-onboarding` after repo → general
implementation after license-validation, parallel with konflux). Dashboard, Platform
Operator, Notebooks, and Documentation are existing components.

The strategy carries one genuine unknown — which Feast deployment topology to productize

Operator integration and the Dashboard endpoint surfacing build against, so it becomes a
blocking Investigation (E001) with two bounded conditional branches (E010 in each branch).
